title: The Decimal Workshop
objective: Explain the value of tenths and hundredths using a consistent whole.

segments.text: In three point four seven, is the four or the seven worth more? Let's build it.
Each tile is one whole. Here are three wholes. Let's look closely at the next tile.
Divide it into ten equal strips. Four strips are four tenths: zero point four.
Divide each strip into ten equal squares. Seven little squares are seven hundredths: zero point zero seven.
Four tenths cover forty hundredths. That's more than seven hundredths. The four has the greater value.
Your turn. In two point six three, what is the value of the three?
Three hundredths: zero point zero three. A digit's place tells us its value.
